title: Built and tested
detail: ISRO released these pictures on 22 May 2023, a week before launch. It has not published the dates of the tests themselves.
picture: GSLV-F12, NVS-01 - Second-generation navigation satellite NVS-01(aka IRNSS-1J) before encapsulation.webp
source_name: ISRO, GSLV-F12/NVS-01 mission brochure

title: Launch on GSLV-F12
detail: Lift-off from Sriharikota at 10:42 India time.
source_name: ISRO, GSLV-F12/NVS-01 mission brochure

title: Separated in transfer orbit
detail: About 19 minutes after lift-off, in a geosynchronous transfer orbit.
source_name: ISRO, GSLV-F12/NVS-01 mission brochure

title: Orbit raising burn 1
detail: Between these two orbit records the low point rose from 184 km to 8,266 km and the tilt fell from 19.3° to 10.2°. ISRO did not publish burn-by-burn updates for NVS-01.
source_name: Space-Track GP history, catalogue number 56759

title: Orbit raising burn 2
detail: The low point rose from 8,257 km to 21,269 km and the tilt fell from 10.8° to 6.8°.
source_name: Space-Track GP history, catalogue number 56759

title: Orbit raising burn 3 (one or more burns)
detail: The orbit went from 21,180 × 39,921 km to 35,855 × 35,938 km and the tilt fell to 5.0°. The records are four days apart, so this may be more than one burn.
source_name: Space-Track GP history, catalogue number 56759

title: Reached geosynchronous orbit
detail: First orbit record with both the high and low points near 35,800 km, the height of a geosynchronous orbit.
source_name: Space-Track GP history, catalogue number 56759

title: Drift stopped at its slot
detail: The last of three small burns (7, 9 and 12 June) that slowed the drift. The orbit stays steady in the records after this one.
source_name: Space-Track GP history, catalogue number 56759

title: Payload switched on and tested
detail: ISRO has not published when the navigation payload was switched on or tested. It was done before service began.
source_name: ISRO, NavIC presentation to the UN's ICG-17 meeting, October 2023

title: In navigation service
detail: ISRO's slides to the UN navigation committee give 4 July 2023 as the day NVS-01 became operational for NavIC users.
picture: GSLV-F12, NVS-01 - Render of NVS-01 (aka IRNSS-1J) in deployed configuration.webp
source_name: ISRO, NavIC presentation to the UN's ICG-17 meeting, October 2023

title: Built and tested
detail: ISRO released these pictures of the vibration test and the cleanroom on 24 January 2025. It has not published the dates of the tests.
picture: GSLV-F15, NVS-02 — NVS-02 undergoing Vibration Test at 29T Shaker System.webp
source_name: ISRO, NVS-02: Advancing India's Regional Navigation Capabilities

title: Launch on GSLV-F15
detail: Lift-off at 06:23 India time, the 100th launch from Sriharikota.
picture: GSLV-F15, NVS-02 — Pre launch images of integration campaign 10.webp
source_name: ISRO, NVS-02: Advancing India's Regional Navigation Capabilities

title: Separated in transfer orbit
detail: About 19 minutes after lift-off, in a geosynchronous transfer orbit.
source_name: ISRO, NVS-02: Advancing India's Regional Navigation Capabilities

title: Orbit raising could not start
detail: ISRO said the valves that let oxidiser into the engine did not open, so the satellite could not be raised to its slot. It stayed in its transfer orbit.
source_name: GPS World, 'Indian navigation satellite stranded in transfer orbit after valve malfunction', citing ISRO

title: Orbit records show no burn
detail: Over six weeks the low point only crept from 161 km to 187 km and the high point fell from 37,603 km to 37,434 km: natural drift, no engine firing.
source_name: Space-Track GP history, catalogue number 62850

title: Cause found: a loose connector
detail: ISRO's failure committee traced the valve failure to a loose contact in connectors that kept the firing signal from reaching the valves.
source_name: The Week, 'ISRO reveals the tiny glitch that doomed the NVS-02', 26 Feb 2026

title: Built and tested
detail: ISRO released these pictures with the mission brochure on 27 October 2026. It has not published the dates of the tests.
picture_credit: ISRO, via Wikimedia Commons (licence review pending)
source_name: ISRO, GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission brochure

title: Flown with its valves already open
detail: After NVS-02, ISRO opened the pyro valves before launch, so the engine did not depend on them firing in orbit (ISRO's chairman, the day after launch).
source_name: The Week (PTI), 'To overcome technical hurdles ISRO flew NVS-03 satellite with pyro valves open: Narayanan', 31 Oct 2026

title: Launch on GSLV-F18
detail: Lift-off from Sriharikota at 23:51 India time.
picture_credit: ISRO, via Wikimedia Commons (licence review pending)
source_name: ISRO on X, lift-off post

title: Separated in transfer orbit
detail: ISRO: placed in the intended orbit of 170.3 × 38,080 km.
source_name: ISRO, Orbit manoeuvring of NVS-03 spacecraft

title: Orbit raising burn 1
detail: The main engine fired for 2,174.8 seconds, ending at 16:48 India time. Orbit after the burn: 5,477.6 × 37,833.4 km. Health normal.
source_name: ISRO, Orbit manoeuvring of NVS-03 spacecraft

title: Orbit raising burn 2
detail: ISRO has not published this burn. The next orbit record shows 24,551 × 37,763 km and a tilt of 29.1°, up from 20.7° at launch.
source_name: Space-Track GP history, catalogue number 101228

title: Orbit raising burn 3
detail: The orbit went to 34,595 × 35,843 km, tilt 29.9°.
source_name: Space-Track GP history, catalogue number 101228

title: Orbit raising burn 4
detail: ISRO: four manoeuvres in all, 6,164 seconds of engine time. Final orbit 35,765 × 36,196 km (IndianSpaceflight's figure), tilt 29.98° (ISRO).
source_name: The Hindu, 'NVS-03 reaches geosynchronous orbit; satellite in good health', quoting ISRO, 4 Nov 2026

title: Reached geosynchronous orbit
detail: ISRO: the satellite reached geosynchronous orbit at a tilt of 29.98°, in good health.
source_name: The Hindu, 'NVS-03 reaches geosynchronous orbit; satellite in good health', quoting ISRO, 4 Nov 2026

title: Drift to its 111.75°E slot
detail: ISRO's stated destination. Not reached yet.
source_name: ISRO, Orbit manoeuvring of NVS-03 spacecraft
